facts.title: Confucius — Chinese philosopher and educator
facts.text: Confucius was a Chinese philosopher and educator who lived during the Eastern Zhou dynasty.

facts.title: Renaissance in Italy and Florence
facts.text: Italy, and Florence especially in the fifteenth century, was a center of artistic, humanistic, technological, and scientific flowering known as the Renaissance.

facts.title: Leonardo da Vinci — multidisciplinary figure
facts.text: Leonardo da Vinci was a Renaissance artist, scientist, and inventor active in multiple fields.

facts.title: Martin Luther and the Reformation
facts.text: On 31 October 1517, Martin Luther posted the Ninety-five Theses at Wittenberg during the early Reformation.

facts.title: English Bill of Rights 1689
facts.text: The Bill of Rights 1689 established principles including frequent Parliaments, free elections, and freedom of speech within Parliament.

facts.title: 1886 eight-hour-workday movement
facts.text: On 1 May 1886, labor groups called for a general strike emphasizing an eight-hour workday; Haymarket is generally considered important to International Workers’ Day on 1 May.

facts.title: Green Revolution — agricultural context
facts.text: Norman Borlaug’s semidwarf wheat work, together with new genes, fertilizer, and irrigation, supported India’s Green Revolution.

facts.title: Coal and steam-powered factory machinery
facts.text: Steam engines enabled heat energy from coal to power factory or mill machinery; coal-powered steam engines drove nineteenth-century Manchester cotton mills.

facts.title: Iranian Revolution — neutral historical context
facts.text: The Iranian Revolution culminated in 1979 with the overthrow of Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi and Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini’s ascension to power.

facts.title: Velvet Revolution and post-Czechoslovak context
facts.text: The 1989 demonstration in Czechoslovakia started the Velvet Revolution; the independent Czech Republic was created in 1993 after the dissolution of Czechoslovakia.
